buildings.name: Temple of Castor (early Republican)
buildings.summary: Vowed by the dictator A. Postumius at Lake Regillus, where the Dioscuri were seen fighting for Rome and then watering their horses at the spring of Juturna, and dedicated by his son in 484 BC. Danish excavations found its cappellaccio podium, about 27.5 x 37 m.

buildings.name: Temple of Castor (Metellan)
buildings.summary: L. Caecilius Metellus Dalmaticus rebuilt the temple in 117 BC after his Dalmatian triumph on a high podium with a speakers' tribunal in its front, used in the political battles of the late Republic; Verres' notorious contract for its columns (73 BC) is the subject of a speech of Cicero.

buildings.name: Temple of Castor and Pollux (Tiberian)
buildings.summary: Rebuilt by Tiberius after the fire of 14 BC and dedicated in AD 6 in his name and his brother Drusus': octastyle and peripteral with eleven Corinthian columns on the flanks, on a 7 m podium of concrete faced with tufa that held small strongrooms for weights and valuables. Caligula made it the vestibule of his palace. Three columns with their entablature still stand.

buildings.name: Altar and column of Caesar
buildings.summary: Where the crowd cremated Caesar's body on 20 March 44 BC an altar and a 20-foot column of Numidian marble inscribed PARENTI PATRIAE were set up; the consul Dolabella removed them within weeks.

buildings.name: Temple of Divus Iulius
buildings.summary: Decreed by the triumvirs in 42 BC on the spot of Caesar's cremation and dedicated by Octavian on 18 August 29 BC, closing the SE end of the square. A pycnostyle hexastyle front looked down the Forum to the Rostra; in its front a podium with the ship beaks from Actium (the Rostra ad Divi Iuli) enclosed a niche with the round altar on the cremation site.

buildings.name: Regia (archaic)

Rebuilt in the same plan many times.

buildings.summary: Built by Antoninus Pius for his deified wife Faustina in 141, and rededicated to both after his death in 161: a hexastyle porch of monolithic cipollino columns 17 m high, with a frieze of griffins and candelabra, facing the Sacra Via. buildings.name: Temple of Venus and Rome (Maxentian)
buildings.summary: After a fire in 307 Maxentius rebuilt the cellae with back-to-back apses and coffered vaults, walls of brick faced with porphyry and other coloured marbles; the Roma apse survives in the convent of Santa Francesca Romana. Pope Honorius I removed its gilded bronze tiles for St Peter's around 630.

phases.t: admired by Constantius II on his visit

buildings.name: Neronian porticoes of the Sacra Via (south side)
buildings.summary: After the fire of 64 Nero straightened and widened the Sacra Via up the Velia as a colonnaded avenue to the vestibule of the Golden House, lined by porticoes over rows of shops; the brick piers remain along the south side.

buildings.name: Neronian porticoes of the Sacra Via (north side)
buildings.summary: The northern portico of Nero's Sacra Via, later replaced by the Horrea Piperataria and the Basilica of Maxentius.

buildings.name: Arch of Titus
buildings.summary: Single-bay marble arch set up by Domitian after 81 on the summit of the Sacra Via in honour of his deified brother, with the passage reliefs of the triumph of 71 showing the spoils of the Jerusalem Temple, the menorah among them, and Titus' apotheosis in the vault. The first dated use of the Composite order. Later built into the Frangipane fortress.

buildings.name: Arch of Septimius Severus
buildings.summary: Triple arch of Proconnesian marble dedicated in 203 to Septimius Severus and his sons for the Parthian victories, with four large panels of the campaigns and a bronze six-horse chariot on top; Geta's name was erased from the attic after his murder in 212. It stood at the head of the Sacra Via beside the Rostra.

buildings.name: Arch of Tiberius
buildings.summary: Arch voted in AD 16 for the recovery by Germanicus of the standards lost with Varus, spanning the Sacra Via between the Basilica Julia and the Rostra at the foot of the Clivus Capitolinus; a relief on the Arch of Constantine shows it behind the Rostra.

buildings.name: Fornix Fabianus
buildings.summary: The first honorific arch in the Forum, built in 121 BC by Q. Fabius Maximus Allobrogicus over the Sacra Via near the Regia, and restored in 57 BC by his grandson with statues of the family.
